quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Signal and check your mirrors.
Turn your head and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn or change lanes. Check your mirrors and turn your head to look for other vehicles around you.

questions.question: How should a group ride when entering a curve?

options.text: Ride in a single-file formation.
Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in pairs.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Switch to single-file when turning, going around curves, or entering or leaving a highway. Staggered formation is normally better, but not in these situations.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help you avoid serious injury in a crash?

options.text: Wear an approved helmet.
Wear face or eye protection.
Wear protective clothing.
Have a windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a windshield.
questions.explanation: Wear an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing to reduce injury in a crash. A windshield does not prevent injuries.

questions.question: When should you use the front brake?

options.text: Every time you slow down or stop.
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads.
Only when slowing or stopping in an emergency.
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you slow down or stop.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to impair your riding ability?

options.text: Well below the legal limit.
Once you reach the legal limit.
Just above the legal limit.
Well above the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Well below the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Never ride after drinking alcohol. Impairment starts well below the legal limit.

questions.question: When should a motorcyclist shift gears?

options.text: While turning.
Before turning.
While changing power in a turn.
While braking through a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before turning.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn, not during the turn.

questions.question: Where is the horn button on a motorcycle?

options.text: Near the left handgrip.
Near the right handgrip.
Near the left footrest.
Near the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: Know where all your controls are before you start riding. The horn button is usually near the left handgrip.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols.
Blue with white lettering or symbols.
Red and white.
White with black lettering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: How should you position yourself when passing a vehicle on the left?

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front.
Do not signal so you do not distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to pass. Signal your intentions, check for traffic, and pass only when safe. Signal again before returning to your original lane.

questions.question: How can you increase your visibility to other drivers?

options.text: Turn off your headlight during the day.
Wear dark clothes.
Keep your headlight on at all times.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on at all times.
questions.explanation: Increase your visibility by wearing bright or reflective clothing, keeping your headlight on all the time, and varying your lane position as needed.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Change your lane position as needed based on conditions.
Ride faster than usual to reach your destination quickly.
Always use your low beam headlight.
Follow the vehicle ahead as closely as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position as needed based on conditions.
questions.explanation: Be flexible about your lane position, especially at night. Use safe riding strategies when conditions are less than ideal.

questions.question: How should you sit to control your motorcycle well?

options.text: Sit with your arms supporting your body instead of steering.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you must stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to help balance during turns. Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests. Use your arms to steer, not to support your body.

questions.question: What should a good rain suit do?

options.text: Should not be used.
Should not fill with air when riding.
Are not needed since motorcycles should not be ridden in rain.
Should tear easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not fill with air when riding.
questions.explanation: Good rain suits for motorcycles resist tearing and filling with air at high speeds.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign
Railroad crossing sign
Stop sign
Speed limit sign

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. These regulatory signs tell riders what rules they must follow.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is usually located on the left handgrip.

questions.question: The body gets rid of about one drink per hour. If someone drinks seven drinks in three hours, how many drinks are likely left in their system three hours later?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. Someone who drank seven drinks in three hours would have at least four drinks left in their system three hours later.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Reduce your safe space and help others see you.
Increase your safe space and help others see you.
Increase your chance of hitting hazards and let others pass easily.
Reduce your chance of hitting hazards and let you follow closely behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your safe space and help others see you.
questions.explanation: The right lane position gives you more space to work with, helps others see you, keeps you away from hazards and blind spots, and gives you room to escape if needed. Choose a position that increases your safe space.

questions.question: When making a turn, what happens to traction?

options.text: There is less grip available for stopping.
There is more grip available for stopping.
Stopping works the same as on a straight road.
You should never try to stop while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less grip available for stopping.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but be very careful. When your motorcycle leans to turn, some grip is used for turning, leaving less grip for braking.

questions.question: Where do most conflicts between motorcycles and other vehicles happen?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: Most conflicts happen at intersections. Stay alert where other vehicles might cross your path.

questions.question: Is the front brake safe to use?

options.text: Yes, if used properly.
Yes, even if used improperly.
Only if the rear brake fails.
No, it should not be used regularly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if used properly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe to use when used correctly. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least three-fourths of the total stopping power.

questions.question: Before you get on your motorcycle, what should you NOT check during your pre-ride inspection?

options.text: Your tires.
Your taillight.
Your headlight.
Your paint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your paint.
questions.explanation: A pre-ride inspection should include tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn. Do this check before every ride.

questions.question: What is the danger of riding directly beside another vehicle?

options.text: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
It is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
It is safe because you have fewer escape routes.
You should only do this during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride beside another vehicle. You may be in their blind spot. If the driver cannot see you, they may move into your lane without warning. Riding beside a vehicle is also dangerous because the vehicle blocks your escape route if you need one.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It guarantees the driver will yield to you.
It is not worth your time.
It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
It means the driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will yield the right-of-way to you.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to ride faster than the others, what should the group do?

options.text: Let them go ahead and meet at a set place later.
Speed up to stay together.
Split up so each rider can go at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them go ahead and meet at a set place later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster than the group, let them go ahead and plan to meet at a specific location later.

questions.question: What should you NOT do to improve safety when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Reduce your speed.
Use your high beam headlight when possible.
Increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed, use your high beam when no other vehicles are near, and increase your following distance. Watch the vehicles ahead. Their headlights show you the road, and their taillights bounce if they hit bumps.
